transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Iran says only a negotiated settlement can lead to the unblocking of the Strait of Formuz.
On Saturday, President Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait within
the week.
The BBC's Yousuf Taha reports.
Speaking to reporters in New York, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Aracti said that Tehran
was yet to receive Washington's official response through mediators.
Mr Trump had said Iran had only put forward the proposal because it was losing the war.
But, Mr Aracti said that his country would not back down from the conditions it had set
out in the proposal, namely the cessation of all regional fighting, including in Lebanon,
and the lifting of U.S. sanctions.
Meanwhile, the Iranian authorities issued a warning to vessels not to use what they called
unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz, which is critical for world oil supplies.
That's the BBC's Yousuf Taha with our reports.
An early season nor'easter is continuing to pound the east coast this weekend, bringing
high winds, heavy rain, and large waves.
Weather officials say risk from the storm extends from the Carolinas up to Maine.
In Cape Cod, Massachusetts, Sue Mastria says she's grateful to be alive after a tree fell
on her home.
The building inspector came.
He said it's safe, but I'm not sleeping upstairs.
The car took the worst damage, it's totaled.
The storm is expected to continue through the weekend.
In NOLA, it began slipping past Hawaii Saturday, and while weather officials say it could still
cause flash flooding and high winds, much of the expected damage has been avoided.
A hurricane watch has been cancelled, and the hurricane is no longer expected to make
direct landfall.
The Big Island, though, is still expected to see rain totals as high as 20 inches.
Advocates for curbing gun violence are celebrating Governor Gavin Newsom's signing of a slate
of gun safety bills Saturday.
The member station, KQED Lachmi Sarah, reports.
The ten new laws include one that funds intervention programs to interrupt violence, and another
requiring that 3D printers sold in California block attempts to make ghost guns.
There's also one that creates a statewide office of violence prevention.
Mike McLively is the policy director of the Gifford Center for Violence Intervention.
There's a lot of state-level infrastructure now to support cities and community-based
organizations doing that violence intervention work, but we didn't have a designated office,
and this will now create a director of community violence intervention.
The California Rifle and Pistol Association opposed the bill on 3D printing guns, calling
it "a costly, impractical, and constitutionally problematic burden."
For NPR News, I'm Lachmi Sarah.
A major protest was held Saturday in Madrid, where tens of thousands of people marched
in the streets to demonstrate against that country's housing crisis.
The protesters asked for a ban on evictions without alternate housing available and other
protective measures for tenants.
You're listening to NPR News.
Hollywood is riding an encore of Avengers Endgame to a surge in weekend attendance, and as NPR's
Bob Mandela reports, superhero myths aren't the only ones proving to be durable at the
box office.
"Avengers Endgame will have a brief burst of glory this weekend."
"Avengers!
Assemble."
The pushing passed $2.8 billion worldwide, cementing its spot as the number two earner
in box office history.
Tom Holland, one of its many stars, is also in Spider-Man brand new day, which is approaching
$2.5 billion worldwide in spot number three, and he's also in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey,
a more traditional tale of mythic heroes, which recently passed $1.7 billion and still
sells out many of its weekend IMAX performances.
Before it's through, this old-school sword and sandals epic with very few digital effects
has a shot at cracking the all-time worldwide top ten.
Bob Mandela, NPR News.
Parts of Bangkok are flooding this weekend.
Heavy rain that started on Thursday has caused flooding in many areas.
It's also blocking traffic.
Officials have declared the city a disaster area.
Police have set up more than 200 shelters for those displaced by as much as 11 inches
of rain.
The rains are expected to continue through Sunday.
The Vatican says as many as 800,000 people turned out Saturday in Paris for an outdoor
mass.
Pope Leo arrived in the Pope Mobile to the cheering crowd, while there he encouraged
those attending to share their faith worldwide.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Iran says only negotiated settlement can unblock Strait of Hormuz, rejects Trump proposal
Early season nor'easter pounds U.S. East Coast with high winds, heavy rain, large waves
Hurricane in Pacific passes Hawaii, expected to bring up to 20 inches rain to Big Island
California Governor Newsom signs ten gun safety bills including 3D printer restrictions
Tens of thousands protest in Madrid against country's housing crisis and evictions
Avengers Endgame surges to number two all-time box office earner at $2.8 billion worldwide
Parts of Bangkok flood from heavy rain, officials declare disaster area, set up 200 shelters
Vatican reports 800,000 people attended outdoor mass in Paris with Pope Leo
